value.name: name
value.value: ITW-SPAI (SPAI tuned for in-the-wild images)
value.description: Name of the model.

value.name: description
value.value:
ITW-SPAI detects fully AI-generated images and is tuned for images shared on social media ("in the wild"). It is an in-the-wild variant of SPAI (Karageorgiou et al., CVPR 2025), developed within the ITW-SM study of Konstantinidou et al. (MAD '26), and is deployed in the MeVer Deepfake Detection service as "itw\_spai\_mever".

How it works: the image is analysed at its native resolution, without resizing, as a grid of 224×224 patches. For every patch, a frozen DINOv2-L/14 vision encoder represents the patch together with its low- and high-frequency components, and the similarity between these representations (spectral reconstruction similarity) is used as evidence, read in the context of the patch content (spectral context vector). Spectral context attention then weighs the patches and combines them into one image-level score between 0 (real) and 1 (AI-generated).

What differs from the original SPAI: the masked-spectral-learning ViT-B/16 backbone is replaced by DINOv2-L/14, and the model is trained on lab-generated (LDM) and in-the-wild (TWIGMA) AI images, with real images from COCO, LSUN and OpenImages, using strong augmentations. In the ITW-SM study this configuration reaches 98.10% AUC on the ITW-SM social-media benchmark, 97.45% on Synthbuster and 90.21% on Chameleon.

Caveats: the score is not a calibrated probability; the model does not localise manipulations; it is not designed for partially edited images or for derivative copies such as screenshots and re-photographed or printed images; and its training data predate generators released after early 2023.

value.name: use_cases
value.value:
*   Screening still images shared online, particularly on social media, for signs that they were fully generated by AI, to help journalists and fact-checkers decide which images need closer verification. Other channels, such as messaging apps, were not evaluated.
*   Providing one signal among several in the MeVer Deepfake Detection service, next to its other detectors.
*   Research and benchmarking of AI-generated image detection under real-world conditions.

value.name: out_of_scope_use
value.value:
*   Serving as the sole basis for publishing a verdict, for legal or disciplinary decisions, or for accusations against individuals.
*   Treating a low score as proof that an image is authentic, or a high score as proof that it is AI-generated.
*   Detecting or localising partial manipulations (inpainting, face swaps, splicing, retouching): the model gives one score per image and was trained only on fully generated and real images.
*   Video and audio. Memes, screenshots and images with heavy text overlays or watermarks were filtered out of ITW-SM, so behaviour on such content is largely untested.
*   Attributing an image to a specific generator.
*   Automated moderation or takedown at scale without human review.
value.description: Unintended or improper use of the model, for example in scenarios that could degrade its quality.

value.name: software
value.value:
*   Deployed model: nothing to install. It runs on MeVer servers and is used over HTTPS through the MeVer Deepfake Detection API v4 (specification: [https://apis.mever.gr/deepfake/v4/openapi.json](https://apis.mever.gr/deepfake/v4/openapi.json)).
*   Underlying code: the SPAI code base ([https://github.com/mever-team/spai](https://github.com/mever-team/spai)), which needs Python 3.11, PyTorch with CUDA 12.4 and the packages in its requirements.txt (e.g. timm 0.4.12, albumentations 1.4.14, OpenCV, NumPy, pandas); NVIDIA APEX is needed for training. The code includes a DINOv2 backbone option loaded through torch.hub (facebookresearch/dinov2).
*   Third-party software and data keep their original licences.
value.description: Software requirements and dependencies?

value.name: instructions
value.value:
The model can be used only through the MeVer Deepfake Detection API, which works asynchronously:

1.  Submit a job with POST [https://apis.mever.gr/deepfake/v4/images/jobs](https://apis.mever.gr/deepfake/v4/images/jobs) with services=itw\_spai\_mever and either the image address in the "url" query parameter (URL-encoded) or the image file in the multipart form field "file". The response contains a job "id".
2.  Poll GET [https://apis.mever.gr/deepfake/v4/images/reports/JOB\_ID](https://apis.mever.gr/deepfake/v4/images/reports/JOB_ID) until "status" is COMPLETED. The "info.itw\_spai\_mever" object shows the progress: PENDING, QUEUED, STARTED, possibly PENDING\_RETRY, then COMPLETED or FAILED.
3.  Read the "itw\_spai\_mever\_report" object: "prediction" (score) and "label" (evidence level).

```
curl -X POST "https://apis.mever.gr/deepfake/v4/images/jobs?services=itw_spai_mever&url=ENCODED_IMAGE_URL"
curl -X POST "https://apis.mever.gr/deepfake/v4/images/jobs?services=itw_spai_mever" -F "file=@image.jpg"
curl "https://apis.mever.gr/deepfake/v4/images/reports/JOB_ID"
```

Submit the original file whenever possible: a re-shared, downscaled or screenshotted copy has lost much of the trace the model relies on. Several detectors can run on the same image by listing them, comma-separated, in "services".
value.description: Use instructions.

value.name: inputs_outputs
value.value:
Input: one still image, given as a URL or an uploaded file and converted to RGB. It must be at least 256×256 pixels (smaller images are rejected with BAD\_IMAGE\_TOO\_LOW\_RESOLUTION); the service sets no maximum image size for this model. The image is not resized: it is tiled into non-overlapping 224×224 patches, and the border strips on the right and bottom that are narrower than a patch are not analysed (for a 1080×1080 image, about 31% of the area). Images that yield fewer than four patches (e.g. any image smaller than 448×448 pixels yields one) are scored on those patches only; the public SPAI code would analyse five overlapping crops instead, but the deployed service does not.

Output, in the "itw\_spai\_mever\_report" object:

*   "prediction": a score in \[0, 1\]; values near 0 indicate a real image and values near 1 an AI-generated one. It is not calibrated, so it should not be read as a probability or compared with 0.5.
*   "label": the evidence level, VERY\_STRONG\_EVIDENCE, STRONG\_EVIDENCE, MODERATE\_EVIDENCE or WEAK\_EVIDENCE, from score thresholds set on ITW-SM at fixed false-positive rates (see the Thresholds field of the Performance section); it may be null.
*   "version": the model version (currently "1"); "completed": true when the analysis succeeded.

On failure the report contains completed: false, a "message", an "error\_code" such as INTERNAL\_ERROR\_INFERENCE, and an "error\_id".

Example report (abridged):

```
{"status": "COMPLETED", "itw_spai_mever_report": {"version": "1", "completed": true, "prediction": 0.99976, "label": "VERY_STRONG_EVIDENCE"}}
```
value.description: Description of the model's inputs and outputs

value.name: factors
value.value:
*   Processing history: recompression, downscaling, cropping, filters and repeated re-sharing weaken or erase the low-level traces the model relies on. Derivative copies (screenshots, photos of screens, scans of prints) are a known failure case of SPAI.
*   Resolution: larger images provide more patches and more evidence, while border strips narrower than a patch are skipped. Small images yield only one to three patches and are expected to give less reliable scores (not measured).
*   Generator: training covers latent diffusion images and AI images shared on Twitter up to March 2023. Images from newer or unusual generators, upscalers and AI editing tools may be missed.
*   Content and style: performance is lowest on highly realistic, artist-refined AI images (Chameleon, 90.21% AUC). The real training images are mostly photographs, so authentic digital art, illustrations, renders and heavily edited photos are under-represented.
*   Platform: ITW-SM covers Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X; other platforms and messaging apps process images differently.
*   Adversarial manipulation: deliberate post-processing or adversarial perturbations aimed at evading detection have not been evaluated.
value.description: Foreseeable salient factors for which model performance may vary.

value.name: hardware
value.value:
*   Deployed model: runs on MeVer GPU servers; no local hardware is needed.
*   Local inference with the SPAI code: a recent CUDA GPU. The original SPAI (ViT-B/16 backbone) runs with less than 8 GB of GPU memory for typical image sizes. ITW-SPAI uses the larger DINOv2-L/14 encoder (about 300M parameters), so higher memory needs should be expected, and time grows with the number of 224×224 patches, i.e. with image resolution.
*   Training: the SPAI recipe was designed for a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of memory.
value.description: Hardware requirements for training and inference.

value.name: more
value.value:
*   Weigh scores and labels together with independent evidence: reverse image search, provenance metadata such as C2PA, contextual verification, and detectors from other families. Other MeVer detectors such as "itw\_rine\_mever" (same frozen DINOv2-L/14 encoder and same training data) and "online\_spai\_mever" (same architecture, partly the same training data) share much with ITW-SPAI, so agreement among them is weak corroboration.
*   "online\_spai\_mever" is additionally trained on in-the-wild images from fact-checks and on images from 19 recent generators (AIGenImages2026), so it may cover recent generators better; its performance is not covered by this card.
*   The original SPAI model (MFM ViT-B/16 backbone, LDM training data; not this ITW variant) can be run locally with the public code and weights: python -m spai infer --input INPUT\_DIR --output OUTPUT\_DIR.
value.description: Additional information about intended uses not found above.

value.name: datasets
value.value:
ITW-SPAI uses the "LDM+TWIGMA (1.2M)" configuration of the ITW-SM study:

*   LDM training set (Corvi et al., ICASSP 2023; [https://github.com/grip-unina/DMimageDetection](https://github.com/grip-unina/DMimageDetection)): 200K low-resolution images generated by a latent diffusion model and 200K real images from MS COCO and LSUN. The SPAI recipe uses its 180K + 180K training split.
*   TWIGMA (Chen and Zou, NeurIPS 2023; [https://yiqunchen.github.io/TWIGMA/](https://yiqunchen.github.io/TWIGMA/)): 600K of the roughly 800K AI-generated images in TWIGMA, which were shared on Twitter between January 2021 and March 2023. How the subset was selected is not reported.
*   OpenImages (Kuznetsova et al., IJCV 2020): 600K real images of low and high resolution, balancing the TWIGMA images.

In total about 1.6M images, balanced between real and AI-generated.
value.description: Dataset(s) used during training.

value.name: motivation
value.value:
The combination pairs a lab-controlled benchmark with real-world data. The LDM set is the standard training baseline for detectors of latent diffusion images and supplies clean generation traces. TWIGMA supplies AI images that were actually posted on social media, covering many generators, subjects, resolutions and platform processing, and OpenImages supplies real photos of both low and high resolution.

In the ITW-SM study, with the same architecture, adding the in-the-wild data raised SPAI's AUC from 78.93% to 98.10% on ITW-SM and from 72.28% to 90.21% on Chameleon, compared with LDM-only training. Using 600K + 600K instead of 200K + 200K TWIGMA and OpenImages images gave almost the same average AUC (95.25% and 95.26%): the larger set scored slightly higher on Chameleon (+0.83 points) and ITW-SM (+0.51), the smaller one on Synthbuster (+1.36). These are single runs without uncertainty estimates.
value.description: Why were training datasets chosen?

value.name: preprocessing
value.value:
Training follows the default SPAI recipe:

*   Each training image yields four augmented views, each a random crop covering 20–100% of the image area, resized to 224×224.
*   Augmentations, each applied with probability 0.5: horizontal and vertical flips, rotation of up to 90°, Gaussian blur (kernel 3–9, sigma 0.01–0.5), Gaussian noise and JPEG compression (quality 50–100). They simulate the processing images undergo when shared online.
*   Each view is split into low- and high-frequency components with a circular mask of radius 16 in its 2D Fourier spectrum.
*   Optimisation: binary cross-entropy loss, AdamW, base learning rate 5e-4 with 5 warm-up epochs and cosine decay, weight decay 0.05, batch size 72, 35 epochs.
*   The DINOv2-L/14 backbone stays frozen; only the SPAI modules (feature projections, spectral context vector, spectral context attention and classification head) are trained.

value.name: more
value.value:
*   Backbone pre-training: the frozen DINOv2-L/14 encoder (Oquab et al., TMLR 2024) was pre-trained by Meta without labels on LVD-142M, a curated set of 142M images, and was not trained further.
*   Age: the newest training images date from March 2023 (TWIGMA), so generators released since then are not represented.
*   Processing mismatch: the AI-generated TWIGMA images went through Twitter's upload processing, while the real OpenImages photos come from Flickr. The model could partly learn such differences in processing instead of generation traces. The strong ITW-SM results, where the real images also come from social media, suggest this is not the dominant cue, but it has not been tested directly.
*   Licences: TWIGMA is distributed as tweet IDs and metadata under CC BY 4.0, while the images remain subject to the rights of their posters and the platform's terms; OpenImages images are listed under CC BY 2.0; COCO, LSUN and the LDM set keep their own terms. The images can show identifiable people.
value.description: Additional training set information not found above.

value.name: datasets
value.value:
*   Synthbuster (Bammey, 2023): 9,000 images from 9 generators (DALL·E 2, DALL·E 3, Adobe Firefly, Midjourney v5, Stable Diffusion 1.3, 1.4, 2 and XL, GLIDE) and 1,000 uncompressed real photos from RAISE.
*   Chameleon (Yan et al., ICLR 2025): 26,033 images: about 11K highly realistic AI-generated images from AI-art communities and about 15K real photos from Unsplash.
*   ITW-SM (introduced by the ITW-SM study; [https://huggingface.co/datasets/dkarageo/itw-sm](https://huggingface.co/datasets/dkarageo/itw-sm)): 10,000 images from Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and X, kept at their original resolution (0.1 to 45 megapixels) and compression. 5,000 real images come from verified accounts and 5,000 AI-generated ones from accounts and communities that openly share AI content. Real / AI images per platform: Facebook 1,318 / 1,033; Instagram 1,206 / 2,179; LinkedIn 1,269 / 931; X 1,207 / 857.
value.description: Dataset(s) used during evaluation.

value.name: motivation
value.value: The three sets move from controlled to real-world conditions. Synthbuster is a controlled benchmark of generators from 2021–2023 with uncompressed real photos. Chameleon holds highly realistic, artist-refined AI images from AI-art communities. ITW-SM reflects the images users actually encounter on social media, with native resolutions and platform compression; it was built because earlier in-the-wild sets cover a single platform, lack real images, or focus on art.
value.description: Why were evaluation datasets chosen?

value.name: preprocessing
value.value: No resizing is applied before inference: SPAI tiles the image into 224×224 patches at its original resolution (border strips narrower than a patch are skipped), which is why the cropping ablation of the ITW-SM study does not apply to SPAI. ITW-SM was curated with a multi-stage pipeline: images with heavy text overlays, watermarks or non-photographic content (memes, screenshots) were removed, duplicates were removed using similarity scores, and every label was checked manually. AI images whose content hints at their origin were deliberately kept, to preserve the real distribution of AI content shared online.

value.name: more
value.value:
*   ITW-SM is gated on Hugging Face and distributed for research use only.
*   ITW-SM was collected by the team that developed ITW-SPAI. The study compared design options on the same three test sets and reports no separate validation set, and ITW-SM was also used to set the thresholds of the API's evidence labels, so ITW-SM results may be optimistic. No deduplication between the TWIGMA training images (from Twitter, 2021–2023) and the X images of ITW-SM is reported.
*   According to the paper's zero-shot CLIP topic classification, art makes up roughly 44% of the AI-generated images of ITW-SM but only about 5% of the real ones, while people, sports and text/meme images are more frequent among the real ones; real images also have a higher median resolution (Figs. 3 and 4 of the paper). A detector could partly exploit such differences, which would not carry over to other data.
*   Synthbuster covers generators from 2021–2023; the generators behind the Chameleon and ITW-SM images are not labelled, and ITW-SM collection dates are not reported. Performance on generators released in 2025–2026 has not been reported.
value.description: Additional evaluation set information not found above.

value.name: analysis
value.value:
Results are those reported in the ITW-SM paper for the configuration that ITW-SPAI follows.

*   Performance is highest on social-media images (ITW-SM, 98.10% AUC) and on the controlled Synthbuster benchmark (97.45%), and lowest on Chameleon (90.21%), whose highly realistic, artist-refined images remain the hardest case.
*   Of the factors tested for SPAI (training data and augmentations), training data had the largest effect: compared with training on LDM data only, adding the in-the-wild TWIGMA and OpenImages data raised AUC by 19.17 points on ITW-SM, 17.93 on Chameleon and 3.58 on Synthbuster. Tripling the TWIGMA and OpenImages portion (from 200K + 200K to 600K + 600K images) barely changed the average AUC, in line with the study's finding that detectors built on frozen pre-trained encoders gain less from more training data than end-to-end models.
*   Augmentations added 6.64 (ITW-SM), 7.48 (Chameleon) and 2.65 (Synthbuster) AUC points.
*   Under the same training configuration, its average AUC (95.25%) is on par with the study's modified RINE (94.90%, also on DINOv2-L/14): RINE is higher on Synthbuster (99.14%) and ITW-SM (98.23%), SPAI on Chameleon (90.21% vs. 87.33%). Both are clearly ahead of the study's modified DMID (89.46%) and NPR (68.38%) and of zero-shot Gemma 3 IT 27B (79.89%). These are single runs without uncertainty estimates, so differences below about one point should not be over-interpreted.
*   AUC and AP do not depend on a decision threshold; a high AUC does not guarantee few errors at a particular operating point (see Thresholds).
value.description: Analysis and explanation of performance results.

value.name: metrics
value.value:
AUC / AP (%) reported in Tables 4 and 6 of the ITW-SM paper for the configuration that ITW-SPAI follows (DINOv2-L/14 backbone, LDM+TWIGMA 1.2M training data, with augmentations):

*   Synthbuster: 97.45 / 98.00
*   Chameleon: 90.21 / 88.51
*   ITW-SM: 98.10 / 98.35
*   Average: 95.25 / 94.95

Same architecture, other training settings (AUC / AP):

*   LDM data only: Synthbuster 93.87 / 94.17, Chameleon 72.28 / 61.28, ITW-SM 78.93 / 80.17, average 81.69 / 78.54
*   LDM+TWIGMA (400K): Synthbuster 98.81 / 99.02, Chameleon 89.38 / 87.26, ITW-SM 97.59 / 97.80, average 95.26 / 94.69
*   LDM+TWIGMA (1.2M) without augmentations: Synthbuster 94.80 / 94.83, Chameleon 82.73 / 81.02, ITW-SM 91.46 / 91.75, average 89.66 / 89.20

Other detectors on ITW-SM, as modified in the study and under the same training configuration (AUC / AP): RINE 98.23 / 98.50, DMID 92.26 / 92.58, NPR 77.54 / 77.73; Gemma 3 IT 27B (zero-shot) 84.04 / 75.50.
value.description: Benchmark results for any performance metrics.

value.name: thresholds
value.value:
The model outputs a continuous score, and the paper reports only threshold-free metrics (AUC, AP). The MeVer API converts the score into an evidence label using three thresholds set on the real images of ITW-SM, each at a fixed false-positive rate (FPR):

*   VERY\_STRONG\_EVIDENCE: the score reaches the threshold at which 1% of ITW-SM real images are flagged.
*   STRONG\_EVIDENCE: the score reaches the 5% threshold but not the 1% one.
*   MODERATE\_EVIDENCE: the score reaches the 10% threshold but not the 5% one.
*   WEAK\_EVIDENCE: the score is below the 10% threshold; by construction, about 90% of ITW-SM real images fall here.

The rates are cumulative: on ITW-SM, about 10% of real images receive MODERATE\_EVIDENCE or a stronger label, about 5% STRONG\_EVIDENCE or stronger, and about 1% VERY\_STRONG\_EVIDENCE. They say how often authentic images are flagged, not how likely a flagged image is to be AI-generated; that also depends on how common AI images are among the images checked and on the detection rate at each threshold, and detection rates at these thresholds are not reported. The rates were measured on the same data the thresholds were set on and can differ on other platforms, processing chains or content.

The 10% threshold is far below 0.5: in a small API test on 1 October 2026, an AI-generated image scoring 0.0137 was labelled MODERATE\_EVIDENCE, so this threshold is at or below that value. The raw score should therefore not be compared with 0.5. The numeric threshold values are not published.
value.description: If decision thresholds are used, what are they, and why were those parameters chosen?

value.name: methodology
value.value: AUC (area under the ROC curve) and AP (average precision) are computed per test set over all its real and AI-generated images, with AI-generated images as the positive class, and the average is the plain mean over the three test sets. The paper reports a single result per configuration: no repeated runs, standard deviations or confidence intervals. AP depends on the class balance of each set (Synthbuster has nine generated images per real one, ITW-SM is balanced), so AP values are not comparable across sets. The thresholds behind the API's evidence labels were set on the scores of ITW-SM real images at fixed false-positive rates of 1%, 5% and 10%. No independent evaluation of the deployed service is reported.
value.description: Explanation of how metrics are calculated and averaged, with uncertainty measures and evaluation method.

value.name: energy_consumption
value.description: A summary of energy consumption. Unit measuring is a centi-llama, meaning that 100 corresponds to the energy needed per output token by Llama3.2 3B, with greater values indicating higher energy consumption per token. Determines eco friendliness.

value.name: environmental_impact
value.value: Not measured for ITW-SPAI, and no energy or CO2 figures are reported. The ITW-SM study states that all its experiments, covering several detectors and training configurations, took more than 1,000 GPU hours in total. For reference, training the original SPAI on the 360K-image LDM set took about 50 hours on a single NVIDIA L40S GPU; ITW-SPAI uses a training set about four times larger and a larger backbone, so its training cost is expected to be higher. Inference cost grows with image resolution because every 224×224 patch is analysed.
value.description: Report of energy consumption, CO2 emissions or any other environmental impact.

value.name: bias
value.value: Performance across demographic groups (e.g. skin tone, gender, age) has not been evaluated. Content-related differences are likely: AUC is lower on highly realistic artistic images (Chameleon), and the real training images are mostly photographs, so authentic digital art, illustrations or heavily edited photos may be flagged more often. Results are reported per dataset only, not per platform, topic or resolution, although ITW-SM records the source platform of every image and would allow such a breakdown.
value.description: Performance and bias across different groups (e.g. ethnicity, gender)

value.name: ethics
value.value:
*   Data: training and evaluation images come from public datasets and social media posts and can show identifiable people. ITW-SM was collected with a crawler that respects each platform's terms of service and is shared for research only, behind gated access.
*   False positives can damage the credibility of genuine photographs, of their authors and of the outlets that publish them, and can be used to dismiss real documentation of events as fake.
*   False negatives can lend credibility to synthetic images used for disinformation, impersonation or fraud.
*   Recommended mitigations: keep a human expert in charge of every decision; report the evidence level rather than a binary verdict; corroborate with independent evidence such as provenance checks, reverse image search and detectors from other families; analyse the original file; explain the model's limits whenever its output is cited in public.
value.description: Ethical considerations regarding datasets and usage of model, including harmful bias and discrimination concerns. Recommended mitigation measures.

value.name: fairness
value.value: No formal fairness criterion was defined, applied or measured during development. For this task, the relevant notion is that the score should depend on generation traces and not on what the image shows, so that no subject, community, region or style of authentic imagery is systematically more likely to be flagged. Given the topic and resolution differences between the real and AI-generated parts of ITW-SM (see Evaluation), this has not been verified.
value.description: Bias or fairness assessments of the model, for example that indicate discrimination against demographic groups.

value.name: risks
value.value:
*   Design faults: the model depends on subtle low-level traces that compression, resizing and re-capture remove; it gives a single image-level score without localisation; authentic images that share traits with generated ones (digital art, heavy editing, upscaling) can be flagged; the score is not calibrated.
*   Technical faults: pipelines that downscale, re-encode or screenshot images before submission degrade results; very small images provide little evidence; service errors return an error report instead of a score.
*   Environmental threats: new generators and AI editing tools appear continuously, so accuracy decays over time; deliberate post-processing or adversarial perturbations can be used to evade detection; platforms change how they process images.
*   Possible consequences: synthetic images accepted as authentic and spread as disinformation; authentic images wrongly discredited; misplaced trust in automated verdicts.
value.description: Possible threats to the model's validity (design and technical faults) and consequences.

value.name: security
value.value: The model and the service are not certified for cybersecurity, and no compliance with specific security standards is reported. Robustness to adversarial attacks has not been evaluated. Images submitted to the MeVer API are processed on MeVer servers, and the API can match new images against previously submitted ones ("search\_similar"), so confidential or sensitive material should not be submitted without checking MeVer's data-handling terms.
value.description: Is the model certified for cybersecurity or is it compliant with specific security standards?

value.name: caveats
value.value:
*   ITW-SPAI is not the public SPAI release: it uses a DINOv2-L/14 backbone instead of SPAI's masked-spectral-learning ViT-B/16, and different training data, so results for the public SPAI weights do not apply to it, and vice versa.
*   The ITW-SPAI weights are not public, so third parties cannot reproduce its results exactly.
*   The original SPAI paper reports failures on derivative AI images (screenshots, photos of screens, printed copies) whose traces were destroyed; ITW-SPAI has not been evaluated on such images and likely shares this limitation.
*   Only fully AI-generated and real images were considered; behaviour on partially edited or AI-enhanced real photos is unknown.
*   It is a research model deployed to support verification and has not been validated for forensic or legal use.
*   Newer generators may be missed. "online\_spai\_mever", a later model with the same architecture trained on more recent data, is available in the same API; its performance is not covered by this card.
value.description: Additional concerns that were not covered in the previous sections.
